items.text: Abdolali Rahimi Mozaffari described the naval blockade as a trick and said the Islamic Republic should counter it with active diplomacy and military power. He considered negotiation a tool to consolidate achievements. He also emphasized that the enemy attacked Iran with various goals but has failed.

Benjamin Netanyahu, Israel's Prime Minister, called Britain the 'Islamic Republic of Britain.' Manshe Amir, a Middle East expert, said London's interests in the Arab world take precedence over cooperation with Israel. These unprecedented remarks were made against Britain.

The Syndicate of Workers of Tehran and Suburbs Bus Company called for a halt to executions in Iran in a statement. The syndicate condemned political executions and show trials. It also criticized the violation of prisoners' rights in the country.

The Islamic Republic has warned the Syrian government that any military action against Hezbollah Lebanon will face a broad response from Tehran. This message was conveyed to Damascus via Turkey, threatening that more than 100 strategic points in Syria could be targeted. Tehran has also sent this warning to several regional capitals.

In Khuzestan, people complain about very poor living conditions and unemployment. In Tehran, the costs of car repairs and electricity bills have increased significantly. People express grievances about economic pressures and rising expenses.

Pete Hegseth, the US Secretary of Defense, denied reports of poor conditions on the aircraft carrier Abraham Lincoln. He emphasized that necessary facilities are provided for the crew and commanders. Earlier reports indicated that sailors on the carrier intended to jump into the sea due to the long mission.

Hamidreza Zarei, Iran's representative in the 95 kg youth weightlifting category at the Asian Championship in Tashkent, won three gold medals and became the champion. He broke the world record in the clean and jerk with a 214 kg lift. Zarei achieved a total of 378 kg and secured the championship title.

Mohsen Khalasi, a citizen of Sabzevar, has been held in Sabzevar prison for over 390 days without a trial. His case, involving charges such as moharebeh and propaganda against the regime, is under review at the Sabzevar Revolutionary Court. He suffers from bipolar disorder and his lithium medication was stopped after one day.

The Wall Street Journal, citing American officials, reported that the United States is preparing to deploy the aircraft carrier USS George Washington to the Middle East to replace the USS Abraham Lincoln as part of a scheduled carrier rotation.

The Yemeni representative at the United Nations stated that the Houthis have turned the country into a platform serving the IRGC. He called on the Security Council to enforce its resolutions on Yemen and rejected the Houthis' extortion policies. He also said the Houthis are conducting an organized war targeting the lives of Yemeni people.

Jennifer Lokta stated that an Iranian plane entered Sanaa without Yemen government's permission. The flight was meant to transport Houthi officials for Ali Khamenei's funeral but carried IRGC forces instead. She described recent Houthi attacks as part of an organized campaign to maintain regional influence.

The Houthis supported by the Islamic Republic announced they targeted the Aramco refinery with two drones. Yemen's government representative at the UN warned that the Houthis have turned Yemen into a platform for the Revolutionary Guards. This report was published by Troska Sadeghi from Iran International.

Mehdi Moslehi, an oil market expert, said the naval blockade of Iranian ports is fundamentally different from economic sanctions, because in this situation neither Iran's oil can be exported nor can ships carrying goods and oil enter Iranian ports. He added that this American strategy is similar to the approach previously used against Venezuela, and this situation, by reducing foreign currency inflows and worsening the budget deficit, increases economic pressure on the Islamic Republic and will confront Iran's economy with serious challenges.

CENTCOM has started forming the first multi-domain and multinational offensive drone unit called Falcon Strike. This unit will operate with the participation of American forces and regional partners. Official invitations have been sent to regional countries to join this unit.

Behnam Rezaei Malmir, the manager of the Karnameh Jonoub website, who was arrested on April 13, is still being held in Sheiban prison in Ahvaz. His situation in prison remains uncertain. This information was reported by Iran International.

A Houthi-affiliated news agency reported a new drone attack on the Aramco refinery in Jizan port. The attack was carried out with two drones, and Saudi sources have not yet responded. Previously, the refinery had caught fire following a drone attack.

CENTCOM announced the formation of the first multinational and multi-domain offensive drone unit called "Falcon Strike." This unit includes forces from the US and regional partners and integrates offensive drone capabilities in the Middle East. Official invitations have been sent to partner countries to join this unit.
Four men were killed in the village of Mohammadabad Kataki in Jazmourian county. The killings were motivated by honor-related reasons. Three suspects have been arrested in connection with the case.

Takhtam Ramazani, a non-political prisoner in Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad, died due to a ruptured gallbladder and delayed hospital transfer. She suffered severe pain for four days before her death and did not receive proper medical care despite repeated follow-ups. This incident occurred on Tuesday, August 11, 2026.

Galatasaray rejected Al Hilal's 130 million euro offer for Victor Osimhen and stated the player is not for sale this summer. Osimhen has scored 59 goals in 74 matches since joining Galatasaray in 2024. Al Hilal aims to sign Osimhen to strengthen their squad for the Saudi Professional League competition.

Workers of Iran Telecommunication Company and Khazar Plastic protested against unpaid wages and insurance issues. They also complained about improper implementation of job classification plans and threats of dismissal. These problems have caused dissatisfaction and concern among the workers.

According to a report by Israel's Channel 13, CENTCOM Commander Brad Cooper, during his recent visit to Israel and in a meeting with Eyal Zamir, Chief of Staff of the Israeli military, called for resuming war with Iran and attacking its infrastructure again. Cooper said: 'Under current conditions, Tehran will not change its positions; attacking Iran's infrastructure changes the rules of the game and inflicts great damage on them.'

CENTCOM has started forming the first multi-domain and multinational special force called the "Strategic Falcon Special Group." This force is being formed with regional partners and will enhance the military capabilities of member countries. This cooperation will shift the balance of power in the Persian Gulf in favor of the US and its allies.

Jamal Mahmoud Abu Kmeil, a Hamas commander, was killed in an Israeli airstrike on Gaza. The Israeli army and Shin Bet stated that Abu Kmeil was involved in planning attacks against Israel. The strike was carried out to eliminate the threat.

The Tehran Police Information Center announced the arrest of a citizen for publishing targeted content against the country. The charges include promoting despair, portraying society negatively, and disturbing public opinion. This news was reported by Harana News Agency.

In a military exercise in Germany, Ukrainian forces used reconnaissance and attack drones to identify and neutralize US troops and armored vehicles. This exercise became a serious test for the US military against drone warfare. The report was provided by Sadaf Baghbani from Iran International.
Persepolis club released a video featuring Karim Bagheri. The video promises the unveiling of the team's new jersey. This jersey is for the upcoming Premier League season.
Mohammed bin Salman and Brad Cooper discussed defense cooperation and efforts to reduce regional tensions. The meeting took place on August 13. No further details about the talks have been released.

The US Treasury Secretary announced that Washington plans to implement unprecedented economic isolation measures against Iran. These measures include severe economic isolation and a blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. More details will be released next week.

Following the war between the US and Israel with Iran, fuel prices have risen, doubling demand for heavy electric trucks made in China in Asian markets. Exports of these trucks reached 16,823 units in the past four months. Sunny company expects export growth to Asia, Africa, and Latin America to continue.

JD Vance, the US Vice President, stated that the main priority of the Trump administration is to keep oil and gasoline prices low for American citizens. He said the US government is trying to ensure Gulf countries continue oil exports to maintain energy market stability. The next priority is to prevent Tehran from acquiring nuclear weapons.

The Washington Post editorial stated that an agreement with the Islamic Republic rewards its destructive behavior and will lead to instability. The newspaper urged Donald Trump to stop negotiations and continue the policy of containing the Islamic Republic. It also emphasized that economic pressure and oil export restrictions should continue.

Marco Rubio, the US Secretary of State, will visit the US Central Command headquarters in Florida on the morning of Friday, August 14. The US State Department has not released further details about the purpose of this visit.

The US Central Command (CENTCOM) denied reports of seven sailors being killed in a physical altercation on the aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln and an increase in suicidal ideation among the ship's crew. CENTCOM stated in an announcement that none of the personnel stationed on the ship had lost their lives, and the only sailor who fell overboard on August 3 was quickly and safely rescued. The command described the dissemination of inaccurate reports about the USS Abraham Lincoln's mission as an act against military personnel and their families.

Incheon Airport in South Korea became the busiest airport in the world for international passengers in the first half of 2026, handling over 38 million travelers. The increase in transit passengers and reduced flight capacity to Middle Eastern hubs contributed to this change. Heathrow Airport in London and Changi Airport in Singapore ranked second and third respectively.

JD Vance, the US Vice President, stated that the US will ultimately have a stronger hand in the ongoing tensions with Iran and that Iran will not have nuclear weapons. He also pointed out Iran's lack of commitment to its obligations and emphasized that the US focuses on energy issues and military aspects. Vance added that the US has many tools to achieve its goals.

Mohammed bin Salman, the Crown Prince of Saudi Arabia, met with Admiral Brad Cooper, the commander of CENTCOM, in Jeddah. They discussed defense cooperation and regional developments. Efforts to reduce tensions and enhance security were also reviewed.

Kuwait's oil industry has faced a sharp decline in exports after six months of war between the US and the Islamic Republic. This economic crisis is described as the largest since the Iraqi invasion in 1990. Kuwaiti officials warn that continued disruption in the Strait of Hormuz could worsen economic damages.

American officials say the United States has the capability to continue the naval blockade of the Islamic Republic indefinitely. Tehran has conditioned the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz on the lifting of sanctions and the release of its frozen assets. Ship traffic through the strait has decreased, and an attack on two ADNOC vessels has heightened concerns about shipping security.

The Australian Prime Minister called Iran's potential acquisition of nuclear weapons a major regional threat during a phone call with the US President. They also discussed the war, regional developments, and the AUKUS defense pact. Additionally, the Australian Prime Minister requested the removal of US tariffs on Australian goods, which the US President agreed to consider.

Miad Maleki, former head of the US Treasury Department's sanctions targeting office, said internal and political pressures on the Islamic Republic have increased. Therefore, the Islamic Republic is trying to prolong negotiations. The goal is to reach an agreement that it can present as a victory.

Iran and Russia are negotiating to expand cooperation in information security. They aim to advance regulations to bring the internet under government control. These actions are coordinated at the United Nations.

Colombia is dealing with the aftermath of one of the deadliest recent earthquakes. Thousands of rescuers and volunteers have mobilized to find survivors and assist the affected. Some stories go beyond rescue operations, reflecting years of sacrifice and hope.

Bahrain's Foreign Ministry condemned the Islamic Republic's attack on two UAE oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz. Bahrain expressed full solidarity with the UAE and support for its security measures. Egypt's Foreign Ministry also called for an end to actions threatening international maritime security.

The Iranian Human Rights Center announced the death sentence for Sepehr Amirzadeh, a medical student and political prisoner in Isfahan prison. He was arrested at his home on January 13, 2026. His medical assistance to injured people during the Iranian National Revolution has been cited as the reason for the charges.

The football teams Esteghlal and Mes Shahrbabak will face each other on Friday, 23 Mordad 1405, in the first week of the Iranian Premier League. The match will take place that afternoon. A poll about the match result is available on Iran International Sports' Instagram page.

The birthday of the late Abolfazl Zare was held in Isfahan with the presence of his family. His mother said her son turned nineteen but only one bone remains of him. Abolfazl Zare was killed during the protests on January 9, 2026, in Isfahan.

Homayoun Sameyh Najafabadi stated that due to insecurity in the Strait of Hormuz, transportation and insurance costs have increased, leading to a significant rise in drug prices in the country. There are serious shortages and drug smuggling from neighboring countries, especially Turkey. He emphasized that these issues are not the fault of the Food and Drug Organization.

Canada considers Washington's proposal to reduce steel and aluminum tariffs insufficient. Officials from both countries are trying to reach a new agreement before the 50% tariffs take effect on August 19. This issue was reported by Mahsa Mortazavi.

Nigel Farage regained his seat in the UK Parliament in the Clacton by-election with over 22,000 votes. His main opponent was a comedic character named 'Count Binface,' and major UK parties boycotted the election. Farage initiated the election to strengthen his position against financial misconduct allegations.

A tourism activist in southern Iran shared images of local people's spontaneous efforts to clean up oil pollution on the Shib Deraz beach of Qeshm Island. The operation used about 10,000 oil-absorbing pads. Local residents also contributed by providing oil pads, boats, and food supplies.

The Deputy Nursing Minister announced a shortage of about 100,000 nurses in the country. Recruitment in recent years has only replaced retired and departed staff. The Ministry of Health requested to hire 60,000 new staff but has not received a response.

Mojtaba Jabbari, former head coach of Esteghlal, criticized the team's condition and management issues. He said the team's path after being handed over to the Khalij Fars company was unexpected and inappropriate. Jabbari also explained that the team's absence from the playoff match was a decision made by the club's management.

Mohammad Ishaq Dar, Pakistan's Foreign Minister, emphasized the importance of dialogue and diplomacy for achieving lasting peace in a meeting with the US chargé d'affaires. He stated that implementing the Islamabad agreement is the only way forward. Bilateral cooperation between Pakistan and the US and recent regional developments were also discussed.

According to the Jerusalem Post, the Islamic Republic of Iran is rebuilding its infrastructure and missile capabilities faster than previously predicted. Iran has started rebuilding damaged missile centers and bases. Some of its weapons production capacities have also been restored.

Saeed Fattahi announced that Esteghlal football club's transfer window will open on September 4th. With FIFA's approval, Esteghlal can use three player quotas for recruitment. The club has already signed two players and is considering foreign options for the third quota.

Nasrin Kabiri, a political prisoner, is serving a 10-year sentence in Dolatabad Prison in Isfahan. She was sentenced last year on charges of spying for Israel. This information was reported by the HRANA news agency.

The deputy of rehabilitation at the Welfare Organization announced about 145,000 applicants for assistive device subsidies in 1405. Despite a 30% budget increase, there is still a significant gap between available funds and the real needs of people with disabilities. Rising equipment prices and the removal of preferential currency are cited as factors for this gap.

The operation of the Hilton Gravenbruch hotel in Germany linked to Ali Ansari has been halted due to EU sanctions. The hotel's bank accounts have been blocked. Ali Ansari holds shares in two companies owning and managing the hotel.
The family of Yalda Mohammadhani gathered at her grave on her 17th birthday. They recited poetry together and held a birthday celebration. These videos were released by Iran International.

The Minister of Sports announced that the redesign of Azadi Stadium is nearly complete, with necessary spaces created according to FIFA and AFC regulations. The groundwork for the grass has been done, and planting will start in September. Building new stadiums for football teams is not currently planned by the government.

The International Federation of Journalists condemned the 15-year prison sentence for Yalda Moeiri. Anthony Bellanger called for the charges against her to be dropped. Moeiri was sentenced in absentia to 15 years in prison and banned from cultural and artistic activities.

Human rights media reported the arrest of at least seven citizens, including four clerics and students in Mahabad and three Arab Sunni brothers in Shadegan. The identities of some detainees and details of the arrests are unclear. The reasons and locations of their detention are also unknown.

During the funeral ceremony of Hossein Khajeh Amiri, Dara spoke about his artistic status and lasting works. Iraj was one of the enduring voices of Iranian music. This interview was published by Iran International.

The Russian Football Federation announced that the national team will play a friendly match against Iran on Tuesday, 7 Mehr, at Kazan Arena. The exact time and ticket sales details will be announced later. Due to a ban from official competitions, Russia mostly plays friendly matches.

Lotfollah Dejkam referred to the fortieth day after the burial of Ali Khamenei's body during Friday prayers in Shiraz. He stated that avenging Ali Khamenei should become a culture. Dejkam emphasized that the issue of revenge must be pursued until a final result is achieved.

Ahmad Khatami, Tehran's interim Friday prayer leader, said on Friday, 23 Mordad, in Friday prayers that America does not understand the "language of negotiation" and understands the "language of force."

The identities of two victims of the December 2025 protests, whose bodies were left in front of the Qods city governor's office, have been identified. Mehrdad Yaghoubi, a PhD student, was wounded by a bullet, and Mohammad Rostami, an employee and father of two, was killed while trying to help him. This report was published by Iran International.

The 20th Asian Games will be held from September 19 to October 4 in Nagoya and Aichi Prefecture, Japan. More than 15,000 athletes and officials from 45 countries will compete in 43 sports. This information was reported by an Iran International correspondent.

Amirallah Shamqadri, secretary of the Security Council of Khorasan Razavi, reported a clash during the activities of two religious groups in Mashhad. The incident occurred around 22:30 at the beginning of Tabarsi Street and resulted in two injuries. The condition of the injured individuals has been reported as stable.

Ebrahim Azizi, head of the National Security Commission of the Parliament, stated that the US will not be left until its final defeat and it is better for them to flee the region. He added that Iran's decisive response forced the enemy to a ceasefire, marking a humiliating defeat for the US. Azizi also emphasized that by relying on Islamic symbols and lessons from the Ashura school, they pushed back the enemy and preserved territorial integrity.

Andrew Giuliani, former executive director of the White House task force for the 2026 World Cup, expressed strong support for Gianni Infantino and sharply criticized his critics. Giuliani stated that Infantino has taken FIFA to a level previously unimaginable. He also mentioned that the 2026 World Cup generated more than four times the revenue of the previous World Cup.

Donald Trump emphasized his administration's plan to increase economic pressure on the Islamic Republic by resharing Scott Bassett's interview. Bassett announced new measures against Iran to be revealed next week. Washington intends to continue a policy of severe economic isolation and blockade of the Strait of Hormuz.
Nigel Farage won the by-election in the Clacton constituency in East England with over 22,000 votes. He has returned to the UK House of Commons. This news was reported by Iran International.

The Tehran Teachers' Union expressed concern over increased security and judicial pressures on teachers, including summons, imprisonment, and exile. The union called for the cancellation of sentences issued against several teachers. Many teachers are unable to report their situation due to fear of intensified pressures.

On Thursday evening, a clash involving sticks occurred among some attendees in the courtyard of the eighth Shia Imam and religious groups in Mashhad. The Secretary of the Khorasan Razavi Security Council stated that the clash resulted in two injuries. Fars News Agency emphasized that these events took place outside the holy shrine.
Positions of American forces near Erbil airport were targeted by a drone attack. One of the drones directly hit one of the positions. Erbil airport was temporarily closed.

After two rounds of military conflict between Israel and the Islamic Republic, a group of Iranians and Israelis are working to bring the two nations closer. Members of the Cyrus Foundation held a conference in Tel Aviv to announce their plans to support Iranians inside the country. This report was prepared by Babak Es-haqi from Iran International.

The Israeli Prime Minister's Office stated that the Israel-US coalition has weakened the Iran axis. It described the current situation as paving the way for new paths to peace in the Middle East. It also highlighted the importance of the Abraham Accords signed six years ago with the cooperation of Donald Trump.

Benjamin Netanyahu, Israel's Prime Minister, said in a podcast that Britain has become a kind of 'Islamic Republic of Britain.' He made these remarks in response to the UK government's changed stance on Israel and the Gaza war. Netanyahu's spokesperson has defended these statements.

Nima Gholamali Pour asked the Swedish Minister of Justice for an explanation about the influence of agents affiliated with the Islamic Republic and other foreign powers. The Minister of Justice considered these agents a serious threat to Sweden's security. He also announced increased monitoring of foreign financial sources and religious institutions' activities.

Donald Trump emphasized increasing economic pressure on Iran by sharing Scott Bassett's interview. Bassett announced new measures against the Islamic Republic and continuation of the blockade of Iranian ports. This blockade will prevent the entry and exit of goods to and from Iranian ports.

At least two people were injured in a clash among mourners at the shrine of the eighth Shia Imam in Mashhad. The incident occurred on Thursday, 22 Mordad, around 10:30 PM. The injured were taken to the hospital and their condition is reported to be stable.

Ahmad Motahari Asl, the Friday prayer leader of Tabriz, said that the Strait of Hormuz is completely under Iran's control and its economic and geopolitical benefits are being utilized. He added that the Islamic Republic will not give up the Strait of Hormuz and the armed forces are fully prepared. He also mentioned Trump's retreat in the region and the imminent destruction of Israel.

The judiciary of the Islamic Republic has filed a case against Sohail Arabi for humanitarian aid to protesters' families and held a trial. He is accused of "assembly and collusion," based on reports from the Tharallah Corps and his online activities. Arabi's aid included covering medical, educational, and living expenses for families.

Abbas Ghanbari's father dances mournfully at his grave on his birthday in Gooym, Shiraz. Abbas Ghanbari, an engineer and athlete from Gooym Shiraz, was killed by a bullet during protests in front of Gooym police station on January 8, 2026. He left behind a young daughter.
Attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz have resumed. However, commercial ships continue to pass through this strategic waterway. This indicates ongoing commercial activity in the region.

Some citizens have reported a sharp increase in prices and frequent power outages in Iran. The electricity bill in August reached one million nine hundred and fifty thousand tomans. Additionally, a power outage caused the death of a patient dependent on a respiratory device.

Sara Bazoubandi spoke about Ali Ansari's financial activities and his connection to economic networks in the Islamic Republic. She said Ansari's link to Mojtaba Khamenei is just the tip of the iceberg of a corruption and money laundering network. The US and European countries have had information about these networks for years and may target lists of related individuals and companies to increase pressure on the regime.

People in Bandar Abbas held an ancient ritual on the last Wednesday of the month of Safar at the Soro coast. Participants recited Quranic verses and crossed seven waves to send away sorrow and hardships of the month of Safar into the waters of the Persian Gulf. They wished for health and peace in the coming days.

The Israeli army is facing a shortage of about 12,000 personnel, including nearly 7,500 combat troops. To address this shortage, extensive changes in the manpower system have been initiated. The number of reserve forces has increased by about 36% since the start of the war.

In the past week, 81 environmental incidents were recorded in Iran. More than 49 illegal hunters and wood traffickers were arrested, and air quality in 17 cities was declared unhealthy. Drought crisis, waste, and pollutants are other reported environmental issues.

Nabih Berri, the Speaker of the Lebanese Parliament, met with Michel Aoun, the US Ambassador to Lebanon, to discuss Hezbollah's disarmament and the deployment of the Lebanese army in the south. The mechanism for Israel's withdrawal was also reviewed. Berri stated that ending the war and Israel's withdrawal to international borders is a condition for Lebanon's stability.

Esmail Saghab Esfahani explained different scenarios for fuel distribution. One option is to continue the current price and distribute based on queue order. Other options include assigning specific quotas for vehicles and allocating a separate share for public transportation.

Two oil slicks have appeared in the waters of the Persian Gulf near Qeshm and Siri islands. The oil leak near Qeshm is likely from the Minoan Pioneer ship, which was hit by an unknown projectile on August 3. Satellite images and videos have confirmed this issue.

Ahmad Alamolhoda, the Friday prayer leader of Mashhad, stated that holding joyful events after the 40th day of the leader's burial is inappropriate and incompatible with seeking revenge. He emphasized that those seeking revenge should not celebrate but focus on retaliation. Alamolhoda also mentioned that joyful programs would mainly attract the immodest and unveiled.

Shahram Khaledi stated that the US strategy against the Islamic Republic is not limited to economic collapse and the military option remains on the table. The Islamic Republic has mitigated some economic pressures by circumventing sanctions. Currently, both economic pressures and US military actions are intensifying simultaneously.

The deputy of the Environmental Protection Organization announced that the recent oil pollution has affected 9 hectares of coastal waters and over 3 hectares of the shores of Qeshm. Reuters reported observing two oil slicks near the islands of Qeshm and Siri. Naser Karami evaluated the impact of the war between the Islamic Republic and the USA on the region's ecosystem.

In December 1404 (Iranian calendar), during protests in Bushehr, a representative of the province appeared armed in the streets and fired at people. These protests were held in 10 counties of the province following a call by Reza Pahlavi. Farzad Fattahi, a member of Iran International's editorial team, explained the protests and their suppression.

Arian Torvand, a citizen of Mehran and relative of Saeed Torvand, was arrested on August 12 by agents of the IRGC Intelligence Organization. He has been transferred to an unknown location and his status is currently unknown.

The Counter-Terrorism Organization of the Kurdistan Region of Iraq announced that at least three drones were destroyed over Erbil on the morning of Friday, August 14. The attack caused no damage, and the defense systems of the US-led coalition forces intercepted the drones. Since February 28, 2026, more than 965 missiles and drones have been used in attacks on the Kurdistan Region.
